Somatic mutations are not passed to offspring in most animals because they occur in non-reproductive (somatic) cells rather than germline cells [d3,d5,d6,d9,d12]. However, in corals such as Acropora palmata, studies show that roughly half of a parent’s somatic mutations can be inherited by offspring, including via uniparental and biparental reproduction [d1,d2,d7,d8]. In plants, somatic mutations can also be inherited when clonal germ lineages are involved, as demonstrated by crosses within individual clones [d10,d11].
